Governor Ivey Shares a Thanksgiving Message of Gratitude to Alabamians

November 25, 2026

Press Releases

Share

MONTGOMERY – 
Governor Kay Ivey on Wednesday released a video message ahead of Thanksgiving reflecting on the blessings Alabamians may count around their tables.

In her message, Governor Ivey speaks of families celebrating a child’s discovery of the joy of reading, giving thanks for an honest day’s work and welcoming young people home to rural communities where new opportunities await. She also recognizes the service members, law enforcement officers, first responders and healthcare workers whose service will leave an empty chair at some Thanksgiving tables.

The governor also reflects on her tenure, sharing her gratitude for the children who have told her about their dreams, the families who have welcomed her into their communities and the Alabamians who have remembered her in their prayers.

“You took a girl from Wilcox County and entrusted her with the great honor and high responsibility of serving as your governor,” 
said Governor Ivey in her message. 
“Of all the blessings I count this Thanksgiving, the privilege of serving you will forever be among the greatest.”

Script:

My fellow Alabamians:

Soon across Alabama, families will be gathering around the table and bowing heads to give thanks.

At one, proud parents might celebrate a child discovering the joy of reading.

At another, a table gives thanks for an honest day’s work and being able to raise a family right here in Alabama.

In our rural communities, some tables will welcome the familiar faces of our young people, drawn home by opportunities once thought of as out of reach.

And at others, an empty chair remains, reminding us of those whose duty calls them away: Our service members, law enforcement officers, first responders and healthcare workers.

This Thanksgiving is especially meaningful to me, as it will be my last serving as your governor.

I think of the children who have shared their dreams with me, the families who have opened the doors to their communities for me and the countless Alabamians who have remembered me in their prayers.

You took a girl from Wilcox County and entrusted her with the great honor and high responsibility of serving as your governor.

Of all the blessings I count this Thanksgiving, the privilege of serving you will forever be among the greatest.

Governor Ivey also issued a 
Thanksgiving proclamation
 today.
